title: Technology Sector Update for 10/19/2018: SREV, GOOG, OSTK
text:

Technology stocks were mostly in positive territory in Friday's afternoon trade, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 ( XLK ) adding 0.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (^SOX) was falling 1.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) ServiceSource International ( SREV ) rose 46% after it said it now expects Q3 revenue of about $57 million, compared to its previous guidance of $60 million to $61 million. The Street view is for revenue of $60.52 million. For fiscal 2018, it now expects revenue of $238 million to $240 million. Analysts expected $247.91 million for the year. Its results are due on Nov. 7, after market close. Separately, it has also appointed board member Richard Walker as its new CFO, replacing Robert Pinkerton who has left the company.
In other sector news:
(+) Alphabet ( GOOG ) rose some 1% following a report from The Verge report that said Android manufacturers may have to fork over as much as $40 per device to include Google's Play Store and other mobile apps. The report cited documents that it obtained. The new fees for the Google Mobile Services suite of apps, which includes the Google Play Store, vary depending on the country and device type, and will apply to Android devices that are activated on or after Feb. 1, 2019, according to the report.
(-) Overstock.com ( OSTK ) fell 7% after it announced some new executive appointments, including Dave Nielsen's return to the company as chief sourcing and operations officer. Nielsen was formerly co-president at Overstock.com where he led the company's merchandising, supply chain operations and marketing. Nielsen previously was with the company for six years, Overstock.com said in a statement.
